# European GPU price report: October 2026

Published 7 October 2026, rebuilt 29 October 2026. EUR list prices from 6 GPU providers with named EU or EEA sites: 26 price points for H100, H200, B200 and B300, each with site, source and date.

## List prices are a starting point.

Send us your requirement and we'll return up to 3 actual quotes from EU-resident providers within 48 hours. Free for buyers.

What is in this issue: public list prices in EUR, only where the provider's own pages place the GPU at a named site or region in the EU or EEA. Every row shows that site. USD lists are converted at the ECB euro reference rate of 1.1133 USD per EUR (28 October 2026).

In short: H100 on-demand at named EU or EEA sites listed from €2.34 (Taiga Cloud) to €4.26 (Verda) per GPU-hour, median €3.19. List prices are a starting point; term, minimum commitment, storage, egress and VAT change the bill.

## Highlights

1. H100 on-demand ran from €2.34 (Taiga Cloud, Sines, Portugal; Boden, Sweden; Kristiansand, Norway) to €4.26 (Verda) per GPU-hour across 6 providers. The median was €3.19. (Provider price lists, accessed 29 October 2026)
2. H200 on-demand: €3.85 at Crusoe (Iceland) to €5.56 at Verda, median €5.05 across 4 providers. (Provider price lists, accessed 29 October 2026)
3. B200 with a named EU site is rare: only Verda (Helsinki, Finland) lists it, at €7.89 per GPU-hour on-demand. B300 is listed by 4 providers, from €7.50 (Scaleway, Paris, France). (Provider price lists, accessed 29 October 2026)
4. Commitment lowers the rate. Verda's published discounts take H100 from €4.26 on-demand to €3.92 on a 1-year term and €3.20 on a 2-year term. (Verda public price list, accessed 29 October 2026)
5. USD lists are converted at the ECB reference rate of 1.1133 USD per EUR of 28 October 2026. Quotes through Kraftcompute come from providers directly and depend on term, cluster size and site. (ECB euro reference rate, 28 October 2026)

results.title: OVHcloud price increase 2026: VPS-1 goes from €4.49 to €6.49, dedicated servers up at renewal
results.author: Fieldnote Labs
highlights:
OVHcloud raised prices twice in 2026. The first round hit Public Cloud, Bare Metal, and VPS in April 2026. VPS-1 went from €4.49 to €6.49 a month, a 45% rise. The second round hits Gen 2024 and Gen 2026 dedicated servers. New orders pay more from July 1 and August 11, 2026. Existing customers pay more at renewals on or after October 1, 2026. OVHcloud blames the rising cost of DDR5 RAM and NVMe drives. All prices here are OVHcloud public prices in euros, excluding VAT. We do not track OVHcloud on SaaS Price Watch yet. More vendors are on the vendor list.

...

For new orders, the rise ranges from 68% to 652% for memory and from 8% to 166% for storage, depending on the option. The schedule:

- July 1, 2026: new memory and storage option prices for new orders.
- August 11, 2026: new server configuration prices for new orders.
- October 1, 2026: new prices for existing subscriptions, at the renewal date on or after that day.

...

- New VPS, Public Cloud, and Bare Metal orders pay the March 2026 table prices from April 2026.
- Existing subscriptions renewed before April 1, 2026 could keep the old rate for the term chosen at renewal.
- Gen 2024 and Gen 2026 dedicated servers in Advance, Scale, and High Grade, plus Game Gen 2026, go up at renewals on or after October 1, 2026.
- Kimsufi, So You Start, Rise, and generations before Gen 2024 are not part of the second round.

results.title: Three European GPU clouds raised their prices for October, while AWS, Azure and Google Cloud held theirs. | Lindstead
results.author: Lindstead
highlights:
# Three European GPU clouds raised their prices for October, while AWS, Azure and Google Cloud held theirs. | Lindstead · LinkedIn · 2026-10-22T00:00:00+00:00

**Lindstead**.

---

Three European GPU clouds raised their prices for October, while AWS, Azure and Google Cloud held theirs.

On-demand price of one H100 per hour, September to October:
• Nebius (NL): €3.38 to €3.95, up 17%
• Scaleway (FR): €2.73 to €2.87, up 5%
• Verda (FI): €3.09 to €3.18, up 3%

Nebius raised its newest GPUs most. A B300 now costs €8.33 an hour, up 21 percent. OVHcloud and Hetzner did not change their prices.

MSP Business and Dutch IT Channel reported the Nebius increase on 30 September, citing the index.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
# Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16

Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

What it does to the board when it lands: Lambda's B200 at $6.69 is currently the cheapest verified HGX B200 instance rate we list from a self-serve cloud; at $7.69 it would sit above RunPod Community's $5.98 marketplace rate and just below RunPod Secure's $7.99. Its H100 at $4.59 would remain above the board's best H100 SXM offer (TensorDock, from $2.25 at an 8-GPU minimum) but move Lambda from the middle of the H100 pack toward its top. Around-the-clock, the announced rises add about $730 a month per B200, $438 per H100 and $292 per A100 80GB on a 730-hour month.

results.title: Cloud Pricing Goes Dynamic — The Without Surprise Blog
results.author: Timothy O’Brien
highlights:
Cloud prices are moving again, and the movement looks like a change in the pricing regime rather than a run of one-off adjustments. Between September 17 and October 1, Nebius told customers that on-demand GPU rates would rise roughly 17 to 21 percent and memory-backed capacity about 41 percent, effective October 1. 1 2 OVHcloud unbundled local storage and public IPv4 addresses from its Public Cloud instances on the same date, which moved the price of an identical configuration up 1.4 to 21.9 percent depending on size. 3 CoreWeave announced that it has continued to contract new compute capacity at higher prices, on short terms of roughly three to six months. 4 Under all three announcements sits the same pressure: memory. TrendForce’s September 30 survey projects conventional DRAM contract prices up another 10 to 15 percent in the fourth quarter, after a year of much larger increases, with server DRAM undersupplied into 2027. 5

...

Nebius notified customers on September 17 rather than issuing a press release: new on-demand rates take effect October 1. 1 The increases step up by chip generation, about 17 percent on H100 instances, 20 percent on H200, 19 percent on B200, 21 percent on the newest B300s, with AMD CPU rates up about 25 percent and memory-backed instances up roughly 41 percent, the largest single line in the notice. It was the company’s second increase in roughly three months. 2 The stock market read the notice as pricing power rather than distress: Nebius shares climbed about 10 percent that morning, and operators that had sent no note at all caught a bid alongside it. 6 The detail to notice is the memory line. Providers bundle memory into instance pricing, so it rarely appears on its own on a bill. A 41 percent increase on the memory line says the component inside every instance is repricing, not just the scarce GPUs on top.

OVHcloud did not raise an instance rate at all. What changed on October 1 is what the price includes. Local storage and public IPv4 addresses, previously bundled with Generation 3 instances, became separate billing lines, about €109 per terabyte-month for storage and about €1.97 per month for an address, and the total for an identical configuration rose 1.4 to 21.9 percent: a b3-8 went from €37 to €45 a month, a c3-4 from €33 to €41. 3 The company also replaced its Savings Plans grid, cutting terms to 12 or 36 months at 15 and 30 percent discounts, where the old grid had offered 35 percent on a 12-month commitment. Customers already inside a plan keep their guaranteed compute rate until the end of the commitment, but from October 1 the storage and address lines bill at full price, outside the guarantee.

...

1. Yahoo Finance, September 17, 2026: Nebius Group (NBIS) Raises AI Cloud Prices As Compute Demand Tests Customer Costs — customer communication rather than a public release; higher on-demand rates effective October 1, 2026; compute demand as the stated driver.

3. Octave Klaba, OVHcloud blog, October 1, 2026: Public Cloud: Pricing changes as of October 1, 2026 — identical configurations up 1.4 to 21.9 percent; hourly instance prices unchanged; local storage about €109 per terabyte-month and IPv4 about €1.97 per month as separate lines; b3-8 €37 to €45 and c3-4 €33 to €41 examples; Savings Plans reduced to 12- and 36-month terms at −15 and −30 percent effective September 1, 2026; existing plans guaranteed through the commitment with storage and IPv4 outside the guarantee from October 1.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing Index, November 2026: H100 to B300
highlights:
Every month we check the public on-demand prices of specialist GPU clouds to set our own: CoreGPU prices every GPU at least 25% below the market median. This is the data behind that number, as listed on November 4, 2026.

## Method

- One on-demand price per provider and GPU, taken from public pricing pages or price APIs. Prices for 8-GPU nodes are divided by eight.
- Specialist GPU clouds only for the median. Hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle) are listed separately because their prices are 2.5 to 4.5 times higher.
- Monthly cost = hourly price × 730 hours. Prices exclude taxes.

## Median prices by GPU

| GPU | Prices found | Lowest $/h | Median $/h | Median / month |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA B300 | 8 | 6.60 | 8.98 | $6,552 |
| NVIDIA B200 | 11 | 5.43 | 8.19 | $5,979 |
| NVIDIA H200 | 12 | 2.90 | 4.94 | $3,606 |
| NVIDIA H100 SXM | 16 | 1.99 | 3.72 | $2,716 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | 9 | 1.40 | 2.19 | $1,599 |
| NVIDIA L40S | 11 | 0.73 | 1.57 | $1,146 |
| AMD MI325X | 2 | 3.80 | 4.21 | $3,071 |
| AMD MI300X | 4 | 2.59 | 3.22 | $2,351 |

The lowest prices often come from marketplaces with variable host quality or from “starting at” prices that are rarely available. The median is a better picture of what a team actually pays for reliable capacity.

...

## Hyperscalers

On-demand prices per GPU-hour at the largest clouds remain far above specialist clouds: H100 from $6.88 (8-GPU instance divided by eight) to more than $12 depending on the provider, and B300 from $15 to $17.80. Commitments of one to three years cut those prices by 30 to 56%.

## What moved in 2026

- Prices are rising again for flagships. At least one large specialist cloud announced increases of 10 to 26% on H100, H200 and B300 from December 1.
- Clusters cost more than single instances. Multi-node offers are commonly 20 to 50% more per GPU than on-demand single servers.
- Listed is not available. Several providers list GPUs with no deployable region, or “contact sales” for every flagship.
- Fees moved to storage and idle time. Egress is mostly free; stopped-instance storage, public IPs and minimum billing periods are where extra cost appears.
